items.followUp: A 50 kg cyclist experiences a forward force of 180 N and accelerates at 2 m s⁻². Find the friction force opposing the motion.

rubric.why: Uses Newton’s second law to find the resultant force.
rubric.how: Award for applying F_net = ma and obtaining 120 N.

rubric.why: Friction opposes motion and reduces the applied force to the resultant force.
rubric.description: Finds and identifies the friction force.
rubric.how: Award for subtracting the net force from the applied force and giving friction as 80 N opposite the motion.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 40 kg, applied force = 200 N, a = 3 m s⁻².
Net force, F_net = ma = 40 × 3 = 120 N.
Applied force − friction force = net force.
Friction force = 200 − 120 = 80 N.
The force of friction is 80 N, opposite to the motion.

items.followUp: A force of 50 N makes an angle of 30° with the positive x-axis. Find its horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: Resolution means replacing a force by component forces along chosen directions.
rubric.how: Award for stating that one force is split or resolved into components along specified directions.

rubric.why: The horizontal component is adjacent to the angle θ.
rubric.how: Award for Fₓ = F cos θ.

rubric.why: The vertical component is opposite the angle θ.
rubric.how: Award for Fᵧ = F sin θ.

modelAnswer: Resolution of forces is the process of splitting a force into component forces along specified directions.
For a force F making angle θ with the positive x-axis, the horizontal component is Fₓ = F cos θ.
The vertical component is Fᵧ = F sin θ.

items.followUp: A boat travels steadily at 6 m s⁻¹ against a water resistance of 2500 N. Calculate the power of its engine.

rubric.why: At steady speed, the resultant force is zero, so the engine’s driving force balances the water resistance.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the driving force equals 4000 N.

rubric.why: Power is the rate of doing work; for motion at constant speed, P = Fv.
rubric.how: Award for using P = Fv.

rubric.why: Substituting force and speed gives the engine power.
rubric.description: Substitutes and gives the answer with units.
rubric.how: Award for obtaining 16000 W or 16 kW.

modelAnswer: Given: v = 4 m s⁻¹, water resistance = 4000 N.
Since the boat moves at steady speed, the engine force balances the water resistance: F = 4000 N.
Power, P = Fv.
The power of the engine is 16000 W (16 kW).

items.followUp: A wire 2 m long and of cross-sectional area 4 × 10⁻⁵ m² extends by 2 mm under a force of 8000 N. Find its Young’s modulus.

rubric.why: The extension must be converted to metres before calculating strain.
rubric.description: Expresses the extension in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for converting 1 mm to 0.001 m.

rubric.why: Young’s modulus is stress divided by strain, equivalently FL/(AΔL).
rubric.how: Award for Y = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) or its rearranged form.

rubric.why: Correct substitution and evaluation produce the modulus.
rubric.description: Substitutes the data and calculates Young’s modulus.
rubric.how: Award for obtaining 2 × 10¹¹.

rubric.why: Young’s modulus is measured in pascals.
rubric.how: Award for writing Pa or N m⁻².

modelAnswer: Given: L = 1 m, A = 5 × 10⁻⁵ m², F = 10000 N, ΔL = 1 mm = 0.001 m.
Young’s modulus, Y = stress/strain = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) = FL/(AΔL).
Y = 2 × 10¹¹ N m⁻².
Young’s modulus of the wire is 2 × 10¹¹ Pa.

items.followUp: What is a stopwatch? State the least count of a mechanical stopwatch.

rubric.why: A stopwatch is used to measure elapsed time or time intervals.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it measures a time interval.

rubric.why: The mechanical stopwatch’s smallest division is one tenth of a second.
rubric.how: Award for giving 0.1 s.

modelAnswer: A stopwatch is an instrument used to measure time intervals.
The least count of a mechanical stopwatch is 0.1 s.

items.followUp: Describe how to use a measuring cylinder to measure the volume of a liquid.

rubric.why: A level cylinder and an eye-level reading help avoid parallax error.
rubric.description: Sets up the cylinder and positions the eye correctly.
rubric.how: Award for placing it upright on a level surface and reading at eye level.

rubric.why: For most liquids, the volume is read at the bottom of the meniscus.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the scale reading is taken at the bottom of the meniscus.

modelAnswer: Place the measuring cylinder upright on a level surface and pour the liquid into it.
Bring your eye level with the liquid surface and read the scale at the bottom of the meniscus.

items.followUp: A rectangular sheet is 8.4 cm long and 3.2 cm wide. Calculate its area to the appropriate number of significant figures.

rubric.why: Area of a rectangle is length multiplied by width.
rubric.how: Award for multiplying 6.7 cm by 5.7 cm to obtain 38.19 cm².

rubric.why: Both measurements have two significant figures, so the answer is rounded to two significant figures.
rubric.description: Rounds the area appropriately and gives its unit.
rubric.how: Award for 38 cm².

modelAnswer: Given: length = 6.7 cm, width = 5.7 cm.
Area = length × width = 6.7 cm × 5.7 cm = 38.19 cm².
Both measurements have two significant figures, so area = 38 cm² to two significant figures.

items.followUp: Represent a force of 60 N acting towards South of East.

rubric.why: The vector must be labelled with its magnitude.
rubric.how: Award for labelling the vector 80 N.

rubric.why: North of East means a direction between East and North, pointing into the north-east quadrant.
rubric.description: Shows the correct direction and vector form.
rubric.how: Award for a directed arrow from the origin into the north-east quadrant, with East as the reference direction.

modelAnswer: Draw East horizontally to the right and North vertically upward from a common origin.
Draw an arrow from the origin at an acute angle above the East direction; label it 80 N.
No angle or scale is specified, so any acute angle north of East represents the stated direction.
